note: Third-party tools HELEN recommends. HELEN never installs them: 'helen skills external <id>' prints the official commands; review them, then run them yourself. Each entry has the date it was last verified against its own documentation; 'helen lint' warns when an entry is older than 180 days.

items.name: Taste Skill
items.summary: Anti-slop frontend design: typography, color, motion with good taste. Several variants in one repo (design-taste-frontend, redesign-existing-projects, high-end-visual-design, minimalist-ui...).
items.notes: Use only ONE of taste-skill / impeccable / ui-ux-pro-max as your main design skill. Other repos named taste-skill exist (forks and a 'tasteskill' org whose README points to a different owner): install from the repo linked here.

items.name: Image to Code (Taste Skill)
items.summary: Image-first pipeline: generate or take a reference image, then implement the frontend from it.
items.notes: Assumed to be the 'Image To Code' shown in the video, because it is a skill of this repo; the video only shows a GitHub logo.

items.name: Impeccable
items.summary: Design guidance for coding agents: commands, live browser iteration and deterministic detector rules against AI design anti-patterns.
items.notes: Alternative to taste-skill; the carousel recommends using only one. Runs an installer: read it first.

items.name: UI UX Pro Max
items.summary: Searchable database of UI styles, palettes, font pairings, UX guidelines and reasoning rules; supports many agents.
install: npx ui-ux-pro-max-cli init --ai <platform>   # its README lists other agents (Codex, Antigravity, Cursor...); check the exact platform name there
items.notes: This is the 'UI UX PRO MAX' skill older HELEN prompts referred to.

items.name: frontend-design (Anthropic)
items.summary: Anthropic's skill for distinctive, production-grade frontend design that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
items.license: See the skill's own SKILL.md (the repo is mostly Apache-2.0; some document skills are source-available)
items.notes: After adding the marketplace, pick the plugin that contains frontend-design with /plugin; not verified which one.

items.name: web-design-guidelines (Vercel)
items.summary: Reviews UI code against 100+ web interface rules: accessibility, contrast, mobile, performance, UX.
items.notes: Complements the bundled helen-a11y-perf skill.

items.name: Humanizer
items.summary: Removes AI-writing patterns from text without changing its meaning (based on Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing').
install: npx skills add blader/humanizer --global --agent codex   # Codex
items.notes: Pairs with HELEN's AUDIT-ai-trace-erasure-and-human-craft prompt.

items.name: cro-optimization (founder-skills)
items.summary: Analyzes landing pages against 13 conversion-rate-optimization principles: headlines, buttons, forms.
items.notes: Install only this skill; the repo has many marketing skills you may not need.

items.name: seo (ECC)
items.summary: Technical SEO skill, per the carousel. The ECC repo bundles hundreds of skills: install only this one.
install: ./install.sh --target claude --skills seo   # run from a clone of the repo; pattern from ECC's README, skill name taken from the carousel, not verified
items.notes: ECC warns to install only from its official channels (github.com/affaan-m/ECC, npm ecc-universal, plugin ecc@ecc, ecc.tools); re-uploads and mirrors may contain malware. Do not stack several install methods. HELEN already has AUDIT-final-seo.

items.name: scroll-craft
items.summary: Builds premium scroll-driven websites: page grammars, signature interactions, automated verification.
install: # Codex and others: copy the scroll-craft folder into .agents/skills/
items.notes: Ships executable scripts (doctor.mjs, workspace.mjs): read them before running. Respect the performance budget from helen-a11y-perf.

items.name: 21st.dev
items.summary: Registry of 12,000+ React + Tailwind components (shadcn registry format). You pick a block and it lands in your repo as editable code.
install: npx @21st-dev/cli@latest init --client claude   # also: cursor, codex, vscode, devin
items.license: Free tier limited (2 copies/day); paid membership for more. Check per-component terms.
items.notes: Related HELEN prompt: GENERATE-modern-ui-libraries-aceternity-magic-ui.

items.name: Playwright CLI (Microsoft)
items.summary: Token-efficient browser control for coding agents: screenshots, selectors, recorded code. Lets the agent actually look at your page.
items.notes: Useful for HELEN's visual regression and browser smoke test prompts. MCP alternative: playwright-mcp.

items.name: awesome-design-md (DESIGN.md files)
items.summary: Collection of DESIGN.md files analyzing popular brand design systems (also at getdesign.md). Not a skill: a markdown file the agent reads.
install: # Copy a site's DESIGN.md into your project root, then tell the agent to use it.
items.license: MIT (files extracted from public sites, provided as is)
items.notes: Use as inspiration for structure and tokens; do not clone another brand's identity for a client.

items.name: GitHub CLI (gh)
items.summary: Uploads your code to GitHub from the terminal. Step before connecting a host.
items.notes: Create the repo private first; make it public only on purpose.

items.name: Hosting: Vercel or Cloudflare
items.summary: Connect the GitHub repository and the site goes online on every push. Cloudflare (Pages) is the alternative.
install: # Web dashboard: import the repository. No command from HELEN.
items.license: Free and paid plans; check current terms.
items.notes: Set environment variables in the host dashboard, never in the repo. An official Vercel MCP exists: vercel-mcp.

items.name: DESIGN.md format (Google Labs)
items.summary: Format spec for describing a visual identity to coding agents (YAML tokens + Markdown rationale) plus a linter for broken token references, contrast and section order.
items.notes: Used by the HELEN prompt init-creative-direction-and-design-md. Runs from npx without installing globally.

items.name: Inspiration sources (Dribbble, Awwwards, Behance, Pinterest)
items.summary: Where the carousel takes the idea from before writing a line: Dribbble, Awwwards, Behance and Pinterest.
install: # Websites: browse them, save references with URL and a note on what you take from each.
items.license: Each site has its own terms; references are inspiration, not assets to copy.
items.notes: Record the URL and the reason for each reference in your DESIGN.md notes.

items.name: Godly
items.summary: Curated web design inspiration gallery.
items.notes: When verified, godly.website redirected to recent.design, a design inspiration platform that did not mention Godly. Confirm the site is what you expect before relying on it.

items.name: transitions.dev
items.summary: Library of 43+ UI transitions (modals, cards, skeletons, text) and an agent CLI that scans your codebase, scores its motion 0-100 and proposes fixes as pull requests.
install: npx transitions-agent   # scans the codebase and shows a motion score and findings; applies fixes only after approval
items.license: Not stated on the site; has a free tier and a paid Pro. Check terms.
items.notes: Review the diffs it proposes like any other pull request. Pairs with the prompt enhance-motion-polish-and-transitions.

items.name: Animos
items.summary: Browser tool to turn static mockups into web-ready animations for portfolios: pick a template, drop assets, export MP4/WebM.
install: # Web app: no command from HELEN.
items.license: Free at the time of verification; check current terms.
items.notes: Assumed to be the 'ánimos.app' from your message (dictation was unclear). Useful for showcase videos of designs.

items.name: deck.gallery
items.summary: Curated archive of 200+ presentation decks (brand guidelines, pitch decks, agency portfolios) for inspiration.
install: # Website: free preview with email; full archive is a paid Pro membership.
items.license: Paid membership for the full archive; decks belong to their authors.
items.notes: Inspiration for structure and storytelling; do not reuse other people's slides.

items.name: GSD Core (Get Shit Done)
items.summary: Spec-driven development for coding agents: discuss, plan, execute in fresh contexts, verify, ship. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor and more.
items.notes: The original get-shit-done repository was archived in June 2026 and continues here. Use the installer: its README says not to copy files by hand. Slash commands: /gsd-new-project, /gsd-onboard. Beware of unofficial ports with the same name.

items.name: Ralph Loop
items.summary: Claude Code plugin that keeps the agent iterating on one prompt until a completion phrase appears or an iteration limit is hit.
install: # Part of the official plugins repository anthropics/claude-plugins-official. Add and install it with /plugin (exact command not verified).
items.notes: Always set --max-iterations: it is the real safety net; the completion phrase is an exact-string match. Cancel with /cancel-ralph. Third-party variants exist; prefer the official one.

items.name: CodeRabbit
items.summary: AI code reviews on pull requests and in the CLI. Your code is processed by a third-party service.
install: # Its docs suggest: curl -fsSL https://cli.coderabbit.ai/install.sh | sh   -> download and read the script first instead of piping it to a shell.
items.license: Proprietary SaaS; free for open source; the free CLI tier is rate-limited (3 reviews/hour at verification time).
items.notes: Not open source. Do not send private client repositories without permission. See the prompt audit-automated-code-review-setup.

items.name: Roo Code
items.summary: Agent-based coding extension for VS Code. The repository was archived and the extension shut down on 15 May 2026.
install: # Do not install. Its README points to alternatives: ZooCode (community fork) and Cline.
items.notes: Shown in a video as a tool for Antigravity; it is no longer maintained. Kept in the catalog so it is not re-added by mistake.

items.name: Playwright MCP (Microsoft)
items.summary: MCP server that lets the agent drive a real browser: open pages, click, take screenshots, check what the user sees.
items.notes: Its README says it is not a security boundary: do not point it at sites with sensitive sessions. Prefer playwright-cli when a CLI is enough (fewer tokens).

items.name: Chrome DevTools MCP (Google)
items.summary: Lets the agent inspect a live Chrome: performance traces (LCP, CLS), network, console, automation. Its README names Antigravity, Claude, Cursor and Copilot as clients.
install: # Add --no-usage-statistics to the args to opt out of Google usage statistics.
items.notes: Collects usage statistics unless you opt out. Do not open sensitive or personal pages while it is connected. Good evidence source for the audit-performance-budget prompts.

items.name: Context7 (Upstash)
items.summary: Brings current, version-specific library documentation into the agent so it stops inventing outdated APIs.
install: npx ctx7 setup --claude   # or: npx ctx7 setup
# Manual: server URL https://mcp.context7.com/mcp with header Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
items.notes: A free API key gives higher rate limits: keep it in an environment variable, never in the repo.

items.name: GitHub MCP Server
items.summary: Official GitHub MCP: read and change repositories, issues and pull requests from the agent.
install: # Claude Code/Desktop: see the install guide in the repository docs (not reproduced here).
items.notes: Least privilege: minimum token scopes, a separate token per project, never commit it, use read-only mode when you only need to look. Writing tools (merge, delete) should require your confirmation.

items.name: Supabase MCP
items.summary: Connects the agent to Supabase projects: tables, SQL, migrations, logs, docs.
items.notes: Use it against a development project, not production. Prefer read_only=true and project_ref scoping; never share service credentials across environments.

items.name: Vercel MCP
items.summary: Vercel's official remote MCP (OAuth): search docs, manage projects and deployments, read logs, query analytics.
install: claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com   # then /mcp to authenticate
npx add-mcp https://mcp.vercel.com   # detects your installed agents and configures each
items.license: Service (Vercel terms). Beta at verification time.
items.notes: Connecting it gives the agent the same access as your Vercel user. Keep human confirmation on for deploys and purchases, and only trust the official URL https://mcp.vercel.com. Beware prompt injection through logs or web content.
